Given the curve r(t)=⟨2t2,et,2et⟩, find all of the points at which r′(t) and r(t) are parallel.

a
(1,1,2) and (8,e2,2e2)
b
(0,1,1) and (8,e2,2e2)
c
(0,1,2) and (8,e,2e)
d
(0,1,2) and (8,e2,2e2)
e
(0,1,1) and (4,e,2e)
Submit

decision.explanation: r′(t)=⟨4t,e^t,2e^t⟩. Since e^t is nonzero, parallelism requires the proportionality factor to be 1, so 4t=2t². Thus t=0 or t=2, giving (0,1,2) and (8,e²,2e²).

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{2}\,,\,{e}^{t}\,,\,2{e}^{t}⟩$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t,\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ ⟨2{t}^{2},\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ & =c\,⟨4t,\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ \\ ⟨2{t}^{2},\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ & =⟨4ct,\,c{e}^{t},\,2c{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}=4ct \\ {e}^{t}=c{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{t}=2c{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we obtain that $c=1.$ Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2} & =1\cdot 4t \\ {t}^{2} & =2t \\ {t}^{2}-2t & =0 \\ t(t-2) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $r$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the points corresponding to $t=0$ and $2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2(0)^{2},\,{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ r(2) & =⟨2(2)^{2},\,{e}^{2},\,2{e}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,{e}^{2},\,2{e}^{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the points $(0,1,2)$ and $(8,{e}^{2},2{e}^{2}).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding Points Where a Tangent Vector is Parallel to Another Vector
content.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{2}\,,\,{e}^{t}\,,\,2{e}^{t}⟩$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t,\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ ⟨2{t}^{2},\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ & =c\,⟨4t,\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ \\ ⟨2{t}^{2},\,{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{t}⟩ & =⟨4ct,\,c{e}^{t},\,2c{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}=4ct \\ {e}^{t}=c{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{t}=2c{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we obtain that $c=1.$ Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2} & =1\cdot 4t \\ {t}^{2} & =2t \\ {t}^{2}-2t & =0 \\ t(t-2) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $r$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the points corresponding to $t=0$ and $2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2(0)^{2},\,{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ r(2) & =⟨2(2)^{2},\,{e}^{2},\,2{e}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,{e}^{2},\,2{e}^{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the points $(0,1,2)$ and $(8,{e}^{2},2{e}^{2}).$

Question 2
?

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨t,et,e−t⟩ at the point where t=0, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨−1,−1,−1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
b
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,1,−1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
c
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,0,1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
d
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,−1,0⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
e
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨0,−1,1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The tangent line is r(0)+u r′(0). Here r(0)=⟨0,1,1⟩ and r′(t)=⟨1,e^t,-e^{-t}⟩, so r′(0)=⟨1,1,-1⟩. This gives option b for every real u.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at the point where $t=0,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
after.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=0$,  the vector ${r}^{′}(0)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

 

$$
R(u)=r(0)+u{r}^{′}(0),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨0,\,{e}^{0},\,{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨1,\,{e}^{0},\,-{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point 
 where $t=0$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩+u⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 3

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨3t+5,1−t3⟩ at the point where t=0, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨3,−1⟩+u⟨3,0⟩
b
⟨5,1⟩+u⟨3,−3⟩
c
⟨5,1⟩+u⟨3,0⟩
d
⟨3,−1⟩+u⟨1,5⟩
e
⟨5,1⟩+u⟨1,5⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

At the point where t=0, the vector r′(0) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as R(u)=r(0)+ur′(0),u∈(−∞,∞)

First, we find r(0): r(0)=⟨3(0)+5,1−03⟩=⟨5,1⟩

Now, we calculate r′(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(3t+5),ddt(1−t3)⟩=⟨3,−3t2⟩

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=0: r′(0)=⟨3,−3(0)2⟩=⟨3,0⟩

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where t=0 is
R(u)=⟨5,1⟩+u⟨3,0⟩,u∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Tangent Line to a Curve
content.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨3t+5,1-{t}^{3}⟩$ at the point where $t=0,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
content.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=0,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(0)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(0)+u{r}^{′}(0),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨3(0)+5,1-{0}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨3,-3(0)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=0$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨5,1⟩+u⟨3,0⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{2}-t,5-3{t}^{2}⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨-1,2⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-1,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨-1\,,\,2⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨-1,2⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =⟨-c,2c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4t-1=-c \\ -6t=2c\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=-4t+1.$ Substituting $c=-4t+1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6t & =2(-4t+1) \\ -6t & =-8t+2 \\ 2t & =2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
{\begin{aligned}4t-1=-c \\ -6t=2c\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}-6t & =2(-4t+1) \\ -6t & =-8t+2 \\ 2t & =2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{2}-1,5-3(1)^{2}⟩=⟨1,2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(1,2).$

$$

$$

$$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =((1)^{2}-2)\,i+(1)^{2}\,j=-\,i+j,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(-1,1).$
